description: We are a two-member team combining data analytics and software engineering: a Business Data Analytics student  with experience in applied ML, NLP and agentic AI , and a software engineer who builds the application layer. For Flame in Freefall, we are building an AI-powered dashboard that uses retrieval-augmented generation to search, rank and explain NASA’s microgravity combustion experiments. Our goal is to help engineers quickly find the research that matters for fire safety in spacecraft
summary:
We developed AETHERFLAME, an interactive microgravity fire-safety intelligence and telemetry platform built on NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archive (26+ investigations), the ISS Researcher’s Guide to Combustion Science, and historical spaceflight fire forensics.
In orbital freefall (0g) and partial gravity (1/6g Moon, 3/8g Mars), fire defies Earth intuition forming dim spherical flames, burning invisibly as 500–800 K cool flames, and igniting at lower oxygen levels under gentle 1–15 cm/s cabin airflows than standard 1g ground screening (NASA-STD-6001) predicts. AETHERFLAME addresses this challenge by unifying NASA’s scattered combustion datasets into five accessible modules: a Gravity & Ventilation Flame Simulator, an SI Habitat Priority Ranker (for Artemis Moon Bases, ISS, EVA suits, and Mars transit), a Negative Oxygen Margin Flammability Map, a filterable PSI Repository Comparator, and an Apollo/Mir Forensics & Earth Spinoff Explorer.
This platform makes complex microgravity fire science immediately actionable for mission designers, students, and researchers protecting future lunar and deep-space crews while highlighting life-saving NASA fire-safety spinoffs on Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

We built AETHERFLAME, an interactive fire-safety web app powered by NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion database (26+ spaceflight and modeling experiments), the ISS Researcher’s Guide to Combustion Science, and real NASA spaceflight fire history.

Instead of forcing engineers or students to dig through dozens of separate technical archives, AETHERFLAME brings everything into five simple, interactive tools:

  1. Microgravity Flame Lab: Lets you adjust gravity (1g Earth, 0g Orbit, 1/6g Moon), cabin air fan speed (0–30 cm/s), and oxygen levels (14–40% O₂) to visually see how flames change shape and behavior.
  2. Habitat Risk & SI Ranker: Pick a spacecraft or habitat (Artemis Moon Base, ISS, Spacesuit EVA, Mars Transit, or Cargo Ship) and a safety goal (Prevention, Detection, or Suppression) to automatically rank the most relevant NASA PSI experiments.
  3. Flammability & Partial-g Predictor: Charts the "Negative Oxygen Margin of Safety" (1–15 cm/s airflow danger zone) where materials burn in space even after passing Earth's NASA-STD-6001 test, and uses PSI-22 E-FIELD (10 kV) data to estimate partial-gravity behavior.
  4. PSI Repository Explorer & Comparator: Lets you filter all 26+ NASA experiments by ISS hardware (CIR-ACME, CIR-MDCA, MSG, Cygnus) and compare their exact test conditions side-by-side.
  5. Space Forensics & Earth Spinoffs: Connects lessons from Apollo 1, Apollo 13, and Space Station Mir (1997) to everyday NASA spinoffs like 20-pound composite firefighter air tanks, dust-immune mine smoke detectors (U508), lightweight PBI/GORE-TEX turnout gear, and ISS water-mist extinguishers.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Makes Space Science Easy to Use: Turns complex NASA combustion data into clear visual simulations and plain-English takeaways for mission planners, students, and researchers.
  • Catches Hidden Space Fire Traps: Warns designers about invisible 500–800 K "cool flames" (PSI-69, PSI-159), larger floating smoke particles (PSI-102 SAME) that fool standard smoke detectors, and gentle air currents (PSI-26 BASS) that feed fires instead of blowing them out.
  • Protects Future Crews & Earth Responders: Helps engineers prepare for high-oxygen Artemis Lunar Bases (≥30% O₂) while showing how space research saves lives on Earth.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Code & Data: Python, Streamlit (web app), Plotly (interactive charts and flame simulations), Pandas, and NumPy.
  • Design: Custom HTML/CSS (Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono fonts) with a custom SVG spherical flame wireframe and a matte charcoal (#161A1D), obsidian (#1F2429), terracotta copper (#D97757), and sage (#52B788) theme.
  • Deployment & Data: Built in VS Code, hosted publicly on GitHub, deployed live on Streamlit Community Cloud, and sourced directly from the NASA PSI Combustion Repository (psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo).

How It Is Creative & What Factors We Considered

  • Creativity: Instead of static tables or a plain text summary, we designed AETHERFLAME like a live spacecraft flight-telemetry console where you can test "what-if" cabin air and oxygen scenarios in real time.
  • Key Factors Considered: We accounted for the real physical differences between Earth 1g fire tests and 0g/1/6g space habitats—specifically slow HVAC ventilation (1–15 cm/s), elevated oxygen atmospheres (≥30% O₂), smoke particle clumping (0.3–1.0+ µm) that causes false alarms, and the BASS finding that aiming a nitrogen extinguisher directly at a wake flame in zero gravity can pull in cabin oxygen and make the fire worse.
